source.description: Project parser load point where the attacker-controlled mosquitto configuration file is read into the reusable line buffer.
source.note: The libFuzzer harness only writes bytes to a temporary config file and invokes mosquitto_fuzz_main. The scored source is the project parser reading that file through fptr into *buf.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled configuration text enters mosquitto parsing as lines in *buf.; value `*buf`; from `while(fgets_extending(buf, buflen, fptr)){`

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant parsed value: a token pointer into the attacker-controlled line buffer.
tainted_value_origin.note: strtok_r tokenizes *buf in place, so later address tokens point inside the reusable config line buffer unless copied.

sink.description: ASan crash location: mosquitto__free calls free on a bridge address pointer that no longer points to a live allocation.

root_cause.description: Root cause: the bridge address field temporarily stores token, a pointer into the shared config line buffer, before validation can return early. If parsing aborts before the later strdup at line 1020, cleanup treats this borrowed token pointer as owned heap memory.

coarse_trace.summary: Consumes -c/--config-file and invokes config__read on the attacker-supplied config path.
Reads each attacker-controlled config line into a reusable buffer and tokenizes it with strtok_r.
For bridge address directives, stores an address token pointer into cur_bridge->addresses before validation completes; an early error can leave a borrowed pointer in persistent config state.
After config parsing fails, cleanup walks configured bridges and calls config__bridge_cleanup.
Frees each bridge address as though it owns heap storage.
Calls free on the stale borrowed token pointer, producing ASan bad-free.

fine_trace.note: Loads attacker-controlled config file content into the reusable parser buffer.
Tokenizes the loaded line in place; token points into *buf rather than to a separately owned allocation.
Parses the bridge address value from the attacker-controlled line.
Stores a borrowed pointer into persistent bridge configuration. The patch changes this step to duplicate token immediately, so error paths do not leave borrowed line-buffer storage to be freed later.
Malformed attacker-controlled port can return MOSQ_ERR_INVAL before the later line 1020 strdup, leaving the stored address pointer borrowed from *buf.
Frees the line buffer allocation that still contains the bridge address token pointer.
Cleanup assumes each bridge address owns heap storage and passes the stale pointer to mosquitto__FREE.
ASan reports bad-free here; mem points inside/follows from the freed parser line buffer allocation, not a live owned address allocation.

format.name: Mosquitto configuration text
format.contract: Candidate input must remain parser-admissible for broker_fuzz_test_config, through config__read_file_core, while preserving attacker control over token, so execution reaches config__read_file_core and the sink in mosquitto__free.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC is admitted far enough to execute config__read_file_core on the path toward the annotated source/root-cause/sink chain.
